bullets.title: Iran MOU/ceasefire dynamics drive broad market rally: S&P +1.75%, Nasdaq +2.54%, Russell +3.02%
bullets.body: Stocks surged as Trump announced cancellation of Iran strikes following a ceasefire/MOU deal, with oil prices falling mid-single digits and Treasury yields down 8-10 bps. Geopolitical risk remains elevated—Trump later signaled larger strikes tonight and possible Kharg Island seizure—but the intraday narrative was de-escalation. Strait of Hormuz confirmed open for transit.

bullets.title: ECB hikes 25bps to 2.25%, first increase since 2023; raises inflation, cuts growth forecasts
bullets.body: The ECB unanimously raised rates to 2.25% (deposit), citing Middle East energy shock and broadening inflation; staff forecasts raised 2026 inflation to 3.0% from 2.6% and cut 2026 GDP to 0.8% from 0.9%. Lagarde said there is no pre-set rate path and the decision was not an insurance move; JPMorgan sees one more hike in September with risks skewed to additional tightening. ECB is now the first G7 central bank to hike in response to the energy shock.

bullets.title: May PPI +1.1% MoM vs +0.7% estimate; YoY surges to 6.5%, highest since Nov 2022
bullets.body: Headline PPI beat sharply on energy and final demand goods (largest monthly goods jump on record), while core PPI was softer at +0.4% vs +0.5% expected. Portfolio management fees drove over 40% of the services advance. UBS raised its core PCE May forecast to 0.35% m/m from 0.27%. US producer prices are now rising at the fastest annual pace since November 2022 as the Iran energy shock passes through supply chains.

bullets.title: Initial jobless claims rise to 229K, highest since February; labor market softening at margins
bullets.body: Initial claims came in at 229K vs 220K estimate and 225K prior, with continuing claims at 1,795K vs 1,785K expected. Real average hourly earnings fell 0.7% YoY in May, largest drop since 2023, suggesting inflation is eroding purchasing power. FOMC rate decision is scheduled for June 17.

bullets.title: HF positioning: net leverage fell to 8th percentile; tech dip-buying emerging; Financials shift from sold to bought
bullets.body: HF net leverage fell 4% to the 8th percentile on a 12-month basis; Mag7 saw -2.3z long-side selling but Semis reversed from -selling to +3z net buying over two days and Hardware was bought +1.7z over 5 days. Financials ETFs flipped from most sold to most bought week-over-week, with positioning near multi-year lows; banks averaged +5.7% in July over last 5 years. CTA equity positioning pulled back across regions.

bullets.title: OBBBA tax legislation: S&P 500 FCF could rise 1%+ in 2026; hyperscalers key beneficiaries
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley notes the OBBBA restores bonus depreciation, allows immediate R&D expensing, and provides FDDEI, which should reduce median cash tax rates after their ~3% fall in 2025. Hyperscalers benefit most given large R&D bases and heavy AI capex eligible for bonus depreciation; lower corporate tax receipts also ease Treasury issuance pressures.

bullets.title: World Bank cuts 2026 global GDP to 2.5%; commodity prices revised up 22%; severe energy disruption scenario could take GDP to 1.3%
bullets.body: The World Bank trimmed its 2026 global GDP forecast to 2.5% from 2.6%, attributing the cut to Middle East war impact, while raising commodity price projections by 22% vs a prior -7% forecast. An adverse energy disruption scenario could reduce global growth to 1.3%. China 2026 GDP revised down to 4.2% from 4.4%; emerging markets cut to 3.6% from 4.4%.

bullets.title: IMF cuts eurozone 2026 GDP to 0.9%, raises inflation to 2.8%; ECB may need further hikes
bullets.body: The IMF lowered its 2026 eurozone growth forecast to 0.9% from 1.1% in April and raised inflation to 2.8% from 2.6%, signaling stagflationary pressure. The IMF also suggested the ECB may need to continue raising rates beyond Thursday's decision.

bullets.title: Morgan Stanley credit: CDX realized vol rising; midterm-linked downside hedges well-supported; payer spreads favored
bullets.body: Realized vol in CDX IG and HY has trended higher in recent sessions (5-day IG ~1bp), while ATM implied vols remain cheap vs history. Fast money is supporting IG downside vol in Oct/Nov around midterm event risk. MS sales desk favors payer spreads as cheap convexity funded by selling OTM payers; IG/HY 50-delta 4m2m calendars near 80-90th percentile on 5Y lookback.

bullets.title: Sector rotation: Semis +7.9% lead; Renewables surge on tariff/nuclear catalysts; Software -1.5% on ORCL drag
bullets.body: Semis led equity markets with all SOX components higher; FSLR +8.8% on Section 232 polysilicon tariff outcome; OKLO +7.1% after DOE Aurora safety approval; ENPH +8.6%, BE +6.2%. Software fell 1.5% as ORCL's capex-driven guidance weighed on SaaS sentiment. Airlines rallied ~8% on Iran de-escalation. Industrials +3.35% vs S&P +1.75%.

bullets.title: SpaceX IPO: $75B offering with $5B+ BlackRock order, $70B+ retail demand; Morningstar sees fair value at $63 vs $135 offer price
bullets.body: SpaceX's IPO is expected to raise $75B in the largest public offering ever, with BlackRock placing orders of at least $5B and retail orders exceeding $70B, with a 20%+ retail allocation reserved. Morningstar puts fair value at $63 vs the expected $135 offer price; Oppenheimer initiated at Outperform with a $190 PT. Some market observers note rotation out of GOOGL, AMZN, MSFT, META into SpaceX.

bullets.title: Anthropic pursues first data center leases, seeks Google backing for payments; adds to AI infra demand narrative
bullets.body: Anthropic is pursuing its first data center lease agreements and approaching Google to backstop lease payments, per The Information. This follows Crusoe being pushed aside from a Wyoming AI project after Google raised concerns. KKR launched Helix Digital Infrastructure with $10B+ committed capital anchored by NVIDIA, Vistra, and Kuwait Investment Authority.

bullets.title: May CPI aftermath: inflation eroding lower-income purchasing power; gas spike squeezes sub-$30K cohort most
bullets.body: Citi's restaurant team notes May CPI shows gas prices surging and eroding discretionary spending, particularly for consumers earning below $30K. FAFH inflation (+3.5% YoY) continues to outpace FAH (+2.8% YoY), and the gap widened 80bps vs 60bps in April. Aggregate purchasing power slowed across all income cohorts, though above-$50K households still show positive growth.

bullets.title: BofA consumer card data: spending +5.1% YoY in May, strongest months; Misery Index at cycle high of 8.5%
bullets.body: BofA reports total consumer card spending rose 5.1% YoY in May, described as 'remarkably robust' and the strongest growth in months. Contradicting that signal, the Misery Index (CPI YoY + unemployment rate) hit a cycle high of 8.5% in May as real average hourly earnings fell 0.7% YoY, the worst drop since 2023.

bullets.title: GOOGL TPU v10 production mulled at Samsung 2nm, potentially diversifying away from TSMC
bullets.body: Per The Information, Google is considering using Samsung's 2nm foundry process for the I/O die of its TPU v10 (Icefish) chip, which would mark a notable shift away from TSMC for advanced AI chip manufacturing and further diversify Google's foundry base.

bullets.title: 2026 YTD regime: EM/Int'l and small-cap value beating Mag7, which is down on the year
bullets.body: Multiple sources confirm the 2026 YTD pattern: international and EM stocks outperforming US large caps, small/mid-caps beating large caps, value outperforming growth, and the Magnificent Seven down on the year. Only GOOGL and NVDA have outperformed the S&P 500 YTD in the Mag7 cohort. Bitcoin (-30%) and gold (-6%) are both negative YTD.

bullets.title: Fed: no imminent rate cuts; FOMC June 17 decision looms; hike odds surfacing with new Chair Warsh
bullets.body: Market commentary signals Fed hike odds surging as new Chair Kevin Warsh faces pressure from inflation data (PPI at 6.5%, Misery Index at cycle high) vs. Trump's preference for lower rates. JPMorgan's macro calendar flags the June 17 FOMC as the key near-term catalyst; Morgan Stanley's labor model sees unemployment potentially declining to 4.0% from 4.3% if payrolls run at 100K/month.

bullets.title: Single-stock hedging costs at record premium vs. broad market as vol gap widens
bullets.body: The gap between single-stock implied volatility and index volatility has reached an all-time high, with investors paying record premiums to hedge individual names rather than broad indices. This signals elevated dispersion risk and selective positioning rather than macro hedging.

bullets.title: GOOGL search share at 90.5% globally; CVNA web traffic +61% YoY; ChatGPT holds #1 app download for 17th month
bullets.body: Citi's May internet traffic update shows GOOGL gaining 50bps MoM in global search share to 90.5%; CVNA web traffic growth accelerated to +61% YoY; DASH U.S. MAUs +6% YoY; ABNB downloads +31% YoY; UBER global MAUs +8% YoY. ChatGPT held the #1 download spot for the 17th consecutive month with downloads +16% MoM. Meta core apps (FB/IG/WA) U.S. MAUs declined 1.3% YoY.

bullets.title: Investment banking fees tracking in-line for 2Q; M&A volume +44% YoY; capital markets activity skewing positive
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley reports 2Q26 IB fees tracking in-line with BAC guiding ~$1.8B (+20% YoY) and Citi guiding mid-teens YoY growth. Announced M&A volume is up 44% YoY QTD with completed volume accelerating to +34% YoY. Boutiques (EVR, LAZ, MC) report strong pipelines; sponsor deals lagging but expected to improve.
